subject.declared_domain: The ontology rail between C2 and C3: the OBLIGATION a motif or system carries -- delivery cadence, completeness-over-a-scope, canonical-source, layer-grammar. The INTENT half of INTENT_DENOMINATOR_SYNCHRONIZATION, sourced from ABOVE (a governed contract) and NEVER from the artifact being checked. This card covers the rail's declared vocabulary and its instance population, not the C2 or C3 rungs.

as_of.graph_vintage: Not applicable to the instance population, which is EMPTY. The rail's graph_evidence counts share the 2026-07-23 vintage of its siblings.

methodology.how: The rail is HAND-AUTHORED in the ontology rule bank. It names the obligation TYPE so the intent-source is explicit, fixes a contract_record vocabulary (CORE fixes the terms; ESTATE WS-E1 declares INSTANCES against it and adds no terms), and derives a typed-violation set from the pairing of an obligation with a D2 path. Its seeds are pre-existing proto-obligations: PSTMRT's completeness axis, TRIGGER_LAYER doctrine, and the MDPF delivery-cadence contract (T-1 by 02:00Z) as a written instance.

key.identity_space: TWO spaces at different levels, and only one is populated. (a) The obligation TYPE space: 4 declared tokens in the rail's own vocabulary. (b) The obligation INSTANCE space: a contract_record per contracted resource, keyed in ESTATE WS-E1's registry -- DECLARED BUT NOT BUILT.
key.key_expression: For the populated space (a): the YAML MAPPING KEY under `dynamic_rails.D3_contract_obligation.obligation_types` in org/modules/graph/NFRA_ONTOLOGY_RULE_BANK.yaml. Each key IS an obligation type token -- delivery_cadence, completeness, canonical_source, layer_grammar. A consumer computes a type's key by walking that path and taking the mapping keys; no parse and no derivation. There is NO expression for space (b), because no instance exists and no registry declares one; a consumer needing an instance key must wait for ESTATE WS-E1 or mint one, and the rail declares no minting rule.
key.declared_mapping: PARTIAL BY CONSTRUCTION. The contract_record fixes the fields an instance must carry (required: intent_source, obligation, lifecycle_class, revalidate_by, locality; optional: successor, expiry_condition, cadence, vintage_probe, describes), so the SHAPE of the type-to-instance mapping is declared. What is not declared is the instance KEY: nothing states what identifies one contract_record from another. The rail is explicit that CORE fixes the vocabulary and ESTATE WS-E1 declares instances against it 'and adds no terms' -- which means the instance key grammar is owed by a component that does not exist.
key.evidence: key_expression is MEASURED and exercised on real members: walking `obligation_types` at @5fc45ad69d returns exactly the 4 tokens the expression predicts, and `contract_record.required` / `.optional` were read the same way. The expression is scoped to the space that HAS members and says in its own text that the other space has none -- rather than being marked absent, which would understate a populated type vocabulary, or marked whole, which would overstate an instance space with zero members and no key grammar. v3.1 forbids 'inferred' here and nothing in this row is reasoned from adjacent evidence: every token was read from the subject.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: An UNDECLARED obligation is indistinguishable from NO obligation unless the consumer honours the rail's own rule, and the failure is that consumers do not. With zero instances declared, every completeness or freshness question over the estate today resolves against an absent contract -- and the rail's instruction is that this renders UNKNOWN, never Complete and never a pass. A consumer that treats 'no contract found' as 'no obligation' gets a clean, confident, well-typed verdict of compliance for a resource nobody ever declared a contract for. That is the whole INTENT_DENOMINATOR_SYNCHRONIZATION defect: the denominator silently becomes the artifact's own configuration.
silent_degrade_paths: Zero instances + a consumer defaulting absent-to-satisfied = universal false compliance. This is live TODAY, not hypothetical, because the instance registry does not exist.
A cadence obligation missing from D3 makes D2 forward the cadence, so a freshness derivation returns a value instead of refusing -- the same silent path D2's card records from the other end.

The vocabulary is PROPOSED, not validated: a type that turns out not to fit its corpus will still validate structurally, because structural conformance cannot see semantic misfit. The rail names its own acceptance test and it has not been run.
The lifecycle section declares an enum whose instance population is zero, so a lifecycle query returns empty and reads as 'nothing is in a bad lifecycle state'.
failure_mode.evidence: Every path is stated by the SUBJECT at @5fc45ad69d: coverage_boundary items 1-4 carry the read-from-file reliance, the absence-is-not-absence rule, the zero-instance statement with its 'honest denominator 0 / all-contracted' phrasing, and the PROPOSED-NOT-VALIDATED clause. intent_denominator_binding.intent_from_above states the defect directly: intent must come from a governance level ABOVE the artifact, NEVER the artifact's own config. 'distinguishable_from_true_negative: no' is measured from that: an undeclared obligation and an absent obligation are the same empty read, and the rail says so in the sentence that begins 'the ABSENCE of a declared contract is NOT the absence of an obligation'.

verdict.why: Not QUALIFIED, and the difference matters. D1 and D2 are usable rails with stated limits; D3 is a vocabulary with ZERO INSTANCES whose declared instance home does not exist. Its type space is fully measured (4 of 4 tokens, computable key expression, contract_record shape fixed) and its failure mode is measured and sharp. But the rail cannot yet answer the question it exists to answer -- what obligation does this resource carry -- for ANY resource in the estate, and the component that would let it (ESTATE WS-E1's registry) is not built. INCOMPLETE is the honest standing for a rail that is correctly specified and unpopulated; calling it QUALIFIED would imply a consumer can use it with care, and today a consumer cannot use it at all except to refuse. The rail also declares its own vocabulary PROPOSED and names an acceptance walk that has not been run.
blocking_defects: Instance population is 0 and the declared home (ESTATE WS-E1 registry) does not exist -- owner: the ESTATE WS-E1 lane, not this one.
No instance KEY grammar is declared anywhere; contract_record fixes fields but not identity.
The type vocabulary is PROPOSED, NOT VALIDATED; its declared acceptance test (the WS-C2 walk against MSBEFF's findings) has not been run.

forward_disposition.evidence: The vocabulary is the intent half of INTENT_DENOMINATOR_SYNCHRONIZATION and is cited by D2's cadence sourcing and by the completeness axis. It is incomplete, not wrong; the remedy is population by another lane, not replacement of the rail.
